- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes (e.g., 80→85+), then fails to correct downward — model lags in recognizing peak exhaustion.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds too high a mean after a spike, underestimating subsequent pullback.
- Forecast horizon 10–15 days: model underestimates true volatility and upward momentum.
- Model tends to underestimate true peak values in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window.
- Lagged correction: model reacts too slowly to recent price drops or spikes — often misses 1–2 days of trend reversal.
- Avoid averaging recent high values — model overweights recent peaks, leading to overestimation of future highs.
- When true outcome shows strong upward momentum, model underestimates the magnitude of the rise — especially in the 20–30 day window.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to adjust downward after a peak, even when true price starts to decline.
